Subtitle I: Other Provisions

Health Security Act - Title I: Universal Coverage - Entitles each eligible individual to: (1) the benefits covered under the guaranteed national benefit package of title III of this Act; and (2) be issued a health security card by the qualified health plan (or under the Medicare program or Medicare part C) in which the individual is enrolled. Defines as an eligible individual: (1) a citizen or national of the United States; (2) an alien permanently residing in the United States under color of law; and (3) a long-term nonimmigrant. Excludes from the definition: (1) a prisoner; or (2) an undocumented alien. Deems an individual entitled to part A (Hospital Insurance) benefits under the guaranteed national benefit package.

States that nothing in this Act shall be construed so as to prohibit: (1) an individual from choosing his or her own health care provider; (2) an individual from purchasing any health care services; (3) an individual from purchasing supplemental insurance; or (4) employers from providing coverage in addition to the national benefit package.

Title II: Individual and Employer Responsibilities - Subtitle A: Individual Responsibilities - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to impose a tax, in an amount equal to the Medicare Part C premium liability, on an individual for any month that such individual, or a young dependent of the individual, is not covered under a qualified health plan. Exempts certain low-income individuals from such tax.

Subtitle B: Employer Responsibilities - Imposes an excise tax on a large employer for any employee during any month that such employee was not covered under a health plan or was not voluntarily excluded.

Imposes an excise tax on every employer with respect to the employment of any Medicare Part C covered employee during any calendar month. Treats such tax payments as employer-provided health coverage.

Imposes on every employer an excise tax equal to 80 percent of the applicable individual premium for employees covered under a qualified health plan or for a Medicare Part C covered individual.

Allows employers to treat an applicable percentage of family premium amounts as payment of the employer's employment tax liability. Allows eligible small employers to treat the applicable percentage of their total premium amount as payment of their employment tax liability.

Describes generally excludable employees for which employer contributions are not required, including young dependents, active military, nonresident aliens, employees living abroad, disabled veterans, and religious faiths.

(Sec. 2202) Sets forth reporting requirements.

(Sec. 2203) Requires continued coverage under current group health plans during the transition to coverage under this Act.

(Sec. 2204) Imposes penalty taxes on employers for failure to satisfy certain health-related requirements.

Title III: Benefits - Subtitle A: Guaranteed National Benefit Package - Amends the Social Security Act (SSA) to provide for a guaranteed national benefit package generally consisting of the same benefits for which payment may be made under Medicare to individuals entitled to Medicare part A (Hospital Insurance), and enrolled under Medicare part B (Supplementary Medical Insurance), plus those included below, subject to specified coverage exclusions and cost-sharing schedules detailing annual individual/family health plan deductibles (high and low) and copayments, adjusted for inflation and waivable for certain services.

(Sec. 3001) Includes within such package: (1) limited annual cost-sharing in 2003 for package benefits, with separate limits for prescription drugs in 1996, all adjusted for inflation; (2) unlimited periods of inpatient hospital services in 1988 (when the following enumerated package benefits are also effective); (3) expanded prescription drug coverage (including certain medically-necessary foods) as well as home infusion drug therapy services and enteral nutrients provided as a coverage home infusion drug; (4) family planning, pregnancy-related services, and specified child benefits (including newborn and well-baby services and child hearing aids), with deductibles and copayments waived for prenatal services; (5) expanded preventive benefits for women (including coverage of pelvic exams and screening for certain sexually-transmitted diseases as well as increased frequency of pap smear coverage); (6) expanded mental health and substance abuse benefits providing access to a variety of residential and community services (including group treatment homes and day treatment services), with reduced co-payments for certain children who receive outpatient mental health or substance abuse services; (7) appropriate chiropractic x-rays; and (8) colorectal cancer screening (including colonoscopies). (Includes among such benefits covered package items and services provided incident to qualifying investigational treatment.)

Authorizes the Secretary of Health and Human Services (Secretary) to modify the coverage of immunizations and other preventive services to cover additional services or increase coverage frequency when clinically appropriate and when not resulting in any premium increases under new Medicare part C.

Prohibits a health professional or facility from being required to provide any package benefit if the professional or facility objectives to doing so on the basis of a religious belief or moral conviction.

Directs the Director of the Office of Technology Assessment (OTA) to provide for appointment of: (1) an Advisory Commission on Mental Health and Substance Abuse Services to examine and report annually to the Congress on a variety of issues related to mental health and substance abuse services in the United States; and (2) a National Health Advisory Commission to monitor and report annually to the Congress on the impact of this Act on individuals, employers, and governments.

(Sec. 3002) Requires the Secretary to study and report to the Congress on whether emergency dental services should be included as package benefits.

Subtitle B: Coverage of Outpatient Prescription Drugs and Other Changes in Medicare Benefits - Revises Medicare part B to conform to the package inclusions specified above, as well as make other related changes providing for: (1) payment rules and related requirements for prescription drugs (such as for manufacturer rebate agreements with the Secretary and a point-of-sale electronic billing system); (2) a Prescription Drug Payment Review Commission appointed by the Director of OTA for publishing a guide for consumers and providers on reducing prescription drug costs; and (3) managed care options under provisions on risk-sharing contracts and payments to health maintenance organizations (HMOs). Authorizes appropriations.

Title IV: State Programs - Subtitle A: State Provider Reimbursement Systems - Requires approval of a States provider reimbursement system application only if it meets the requirements of sections 4002 and 4003. Permits a waiver of such requirements relating to the determination of payment amounts under provisions of the Medicare program and under the Medicaid program as may be necessary to implement the system. Prohibits denial of a State's application on the ground that the methodology used under the system to control payments for inpatient hospital services is based on a payment methodology other than on the basis of a diagnosis-related group.

(Sec. 4002) Requires a system to assure the equitable treatment of all payers. Permits a limited payment rate differential under Medicaid that differs from payment rates for services for which payment is made by other payers. Permits a health maintenance organization to negotiate directly with providers of services. Prohibits a State from contracting with a private organization to carry a State's system. Prohibits a State's system from resulting in any change in hospital admission practices or the provision of other service which result in: (1) a significant reduction in the proportion of patients who have no third-party coverage and who are unable to pay for such services; (2) a significant reduction in the proportion of individuals provided services for which payment is less than the anticipated charges; or (3) the refusal to provide services to individual who would be expected to require unusually costly or prolonged treatment for reasons other than those related to the appropriateness of the care available from the provider.

(Sec. 4003) Requires a State to assure that: (1) the sum of the aggregate private sector expenditures and the aggregate Medicare expenditures will not exceed a total specified limit; and (2) the aggregate Medicare expenditures will not exceed the applicable Medicare limit.

Provides for the termination of approval of a State's system if such limits are exceeded.

Subtitle B: State Benefit Management Programs - Permits a State to operate a State benefit management program under which the State: (1) guarantees coverage for at least the guaranteed national benefit package; and (2) controls aggregate health care expenditures as specified. Sets forth general requirements for a State program.

(Sec. 4103) Provides that generally a State may not cover any Medicare part A (Hospital Insurance) or part C (Assistance For Low-Income Individuals) beneficiary under the State program, but permits coverage if the State provides assurances that: (1) all services for which such beneficiaries would otherwise be eligible under Medicare shall be provided under the State system without additional cost to such beneficiaries and shall be reasonably accessible to all such beneficiaries; and (2) such beneficiaries in the State program shall be eligible for the same benefits and provided with the same opportunities with respect to choice of health plans as other State residents.

(Sec. 4104) Sets forth options relating to payment, under a State program, for premium subsidies and wrap-around benefits which be made under Medicare provisions added by title VIII of this Act. Defines State wrap-around benefits as a package of benefits consisting of items and services not covered under the guaranteed national benefit package that is comparable to the wrap-around benefits provided under Medicare provisions added under title VIII of this Act which provide wrap-around benefits for low-income individuals.

Subtitle C: State Comprehensive Managed Mental Health and Substance Abuse Programs - Permits a State to establish a comprehensive managed mental health and substance abuse program under which: (1) the State shall provide mental health and substance abuse services for qualified individuals who choose to receive such services through the program; and (2) such individuals shall receive such services through the programs and not through a qualified health plan, Medicare, or through Medicare Part C providing the guaranteed national benefit package. Requires the program to provide for coverage of the mental health and substance abuse services in the guaranteed national benefit package without the imposition of any limits applicable under the package on the number of days for which the services may be provided.

Title V: Health Plans and Health Alliances - Subtitle A: Standards for Carriers and Insured Health Benefit Plans - Amends the Social Security Act to add a new title, Title XXII - Health Benefit Plan Standards. Requires the Secretary of Health and Human Services to establish standards for carriers providing health benefit plans consistent with this section and the requirements relating to standards for insured health benefit plans.

Requires rules of the standards to be designed to: (1) provide automatic coverage to newborns as of the date of birth; (2) in the case of an individual provided coverage through employment, provide coverage through the end of the month in which the employment is terminated; and (3) prevent eligible individuals from having any periods of noncoverage when changing enrollment among health benefit plans.

Prohibits a carrier from selling, issuing, or renewing a contract under an insured health benefit plan with respect to an individual or employer in a State unless the plan meets the applicable standards of either: (1) the State regulatory program; or (2) in the case of a State without an approved program, the Secretary of Health and Human Services. Defines a health benefit plan. Excludes from the definition of health benefit plan the following: (1) coverage only for accident, dental, vision, disability income, or long-term care insurance, or any combination thereof; (2) Medicare supplemental insurance; (3) coverage issued as a supplement to liability insurance; (4) liability insurance; (5) workers compensation; (6) automobile medical-payment insurance; (7) coverage for a specified disease; (8) a hospital or fixed indemnity policy; or (9) coverage provided exclusively to individuals who are not eligible individuals under the Health Security Act. Defines a health plan as: (1) any contract of health insurance, including any hospital or medical service policy or certificate, hospital or medical service plan contract, or health maintenance organization group contract, that is provided by a carrier; or (2) an employee welfare benefit plan or other arrangement insofar as the plan or arrangement provides health benefits and is funded in a manner other than through the purchase of one or more policies or contracts described in clause (1).

Permits a carrier offering an insured health benefit plan in a State to offer such plan in one or more of the following market sectors: (1) individual market sector; (2) small employer market sector; (3) large employer market sector; (4) association market sectors; and (5) alliance market sector.

Prohibits a carrier from denying, limiting, or conditioning coverage based on health status, claims experience, receipt of health care, medical, history, or lack of evidence of insurability. Prohibits a carrier from discrimination in any market sector based on race, national origin, religion, gender, sexual orientation, language, socio-economic status, age, health status, or anticipated need for health services.

Provides for open enrollment, subject to exceptions.

Prohibits excluding or limiting coverage based on pre-exiting conditions.

Prohibits a carrier from refusing to enroll or renew or terminating enrollment of an individual or employer except for: (1) nonpayment of premiums; and (2) fraud or misrepresentation of material fact.

Requires each carrier offering an insured health benefit plan to offer such a plan that only includes coverage for the benefits contained in the guaranteed national benefit package. Permits a carrier to offer a high deductible plan only: (1) in the small employer market sector and the large employer market sector; and (2) only with respect to an employer making contributions to medical savings accounts.

Prohibits the premium rate charged by a carrier for a type of insured health benefit plan in a community with a market sector from varying, except within the three classes of enrollment, individual, single parent, and married couple and one or more children.

Sets forth special requirements for managed care and point-of-service plans which include the requirement that the plan have reasonably prompt access to all items and services in the guaranteed national benefit package, including access to services on a 24-hour basis where medically necessary.

Requires each carrier providing an insured health benefit plan to offer to enter into a provider participation agreement with respect to each essential community provider which shall provide that the plan agrees to treat the provider at least as favorably as other providers are treated.

Sets forth plan solvency and utilization review requirements.

Requires a carrier to issue health security cards and carry out other administrative functions in accordance with regulations developed by the Secretary.

Subtitle B: Standards for Sponsors and Self-Insured Health Benefit Plans - Continues with additional amendments to title XXII of the Social Security Act by permitting only the following entities to serve as the sponsor of a health benefit plan: (1) a large employer; (2) a plan sponsor of a multiemployer plan; and (3) a rural electric cooperative and rural telephone cooperative association. Applies requirements of Subtitle A (Standards for Carriers and Insured Health Benefit Plans) to such sponsors.

Subtitle C: Standards for Supplemental Health Plans - Continues with further amendments to title XXII of the Social Security Act by prohibiting an entity from offering a supplemental health benefit policy unless the benefits meet requirements for one of the standard benefit packages established by the Secretary. Directs the Secretary to establish not more than ten standardized benefit packages for supplemental health benefit policies. Applies requirements of subtitle A (Standards for Carriers and Insured Health Benefit Plans) to such policies. Makes conforming changes concerning Medicare supplemental insurance policies.

Subtitle D: Transitional Insurance Reforms - Sets forth transitional provisions, including provisions concerning: (1) continuation of coverage; (2) limits on pre-existing conditions; and (3) premium changes.

Subtitle E: Health Alliances - Adds additional provisions to title XXII of the Social Security Act under which the Secretary is directed to make grants to eligible States and to certain units of local governments for the planning, development, and initial operation of regional health alliances. Permits, in the case of contiguous States, making grants for the establishment and operation of a health alliance operated jointly by the States and serving areas in each of the States. Requires each health alliance to enter into a contract with any carrier seeking to offer a qualified health plan that is an insured health benefit plan. Authorizes appropriations. Permits a State receiving a grant for the operation of a health alliance to use funds for the operation of a capital allocation plan in the State by the alliance.

Title VI: Standby Cost Containment in the Private Sector - Subtitle A: National Health Expenditure Estimates - Provides for the establishment of the national private sector per capita health expenditure estimate, to be referred to as the national private per capita estimate.

(Sec. 6002) Establishes classes of health care services such as inpatient hospital services, diagnostic testing services, durable medical equipment, and prescription drugs.

(Sec. 6003) Directs the Secretary to allocate, according to a specified formula, the national private per capita for a year among classes of services.

(Sec. 6004) Directs the Secretary to establish a national health expenditures reporting system to: (1) establish the national private per capita estimate; (2) allocate the national private per capita estimate; (3) determine maximum payment rates; (4) monitor State cost containment and benefit management programs established under title IV; and (5) carry out this title.

Subtitle B: State Health Expenditures Estimates - Directs the Secretary to establish a State private sector per capita health expenditure estimate for each State, to be referred to a the State private per capita estimate.

Subtitle C: Stand-By Federal Cost Containment - Directs the Secretary to annually determine for each State whether the actual State private per capital health care expenditures for the previous year exceeded the State private per capita estimate.

Subtitle D: Maximum Payment Rates - Provides for the establishment and application of maximum payment rates. Defines payment rate as the rate of payment with respect to health care services for which amounts are payable under a plan or program. Enforces such rates through civil monetary penalties on providers. Prohibits fees for medical services charged to insurers from being less favorable than fees for similar services covered under an individual's health benefit plan. Sets forth methodologies for determining maximum payment rates for inpatient hospital services, physicians' services and other professional medical services, services using certain Medicare payment methodologies, services provided by managed care organizations, and other services.

Subtitle E: Administrative and Judicial Review - Prohibits administrative or judicial review of any of the following determinations: (1) the maximum payment rates; (2) the establishment of diagnosis-related groups, the methodology for classification of discharges within such groups, and the appropriate weighting factors; and (3) allocation of the national private per capita estimate or a State private per capita estimate to a class of health services.

Subtitle F: National Health Cost Commission - Directs the President to establish a National Health Cost Commissions to conduct analyses of health care cost and revenue data. Requires an annual report to the Congress and a special report in the year 2000 concerning whether a system of cost containment should be imposed on health care services provided under private health benefit plans.

Title VII: Public Health Initiatives - Subtitle A: Health Workforce Priorities - Directs the Secretary to develop the National Health Care Workforce Plan which shall establish a national goal of developing a health care workforce whose composition reflects the needs of this country for practitioners in the various health professions, including primary care. Requires at least 55 percent of residency positions to be in primary care. Includes obstetrics and gynecology in the definition of primary care.

(Sec. 7002) Directs the Secretary for each medical specialty to make allocations among approved medical residency training programs of the number of residency positions authorized for the year for the specialty pursuant to the Plan.

(Sec. 7011) Provides for payments from the Health Care Workforce Account, established under trust fund provisions of the Internal Revenue Code, to hospitals with approval medical residency training program for the costs of graduate medical education. Sets forth formulas and definitions for determining such payments.

(Sec. 7021) Sets forth other provisions regarding graduate medical education, including: (1) the determination under Medicare of the number of full-time equivalent residents; (2) payments for federally qualified health centers; (3) a study of payments for medical education at sites other than hospitals; and (4) a Medicare demonstration regarding consortia of hospitals.

Subtitle B: Additional Provisions Regarding Primary Care - Amends title XVIII (Medicare) of the Social Security Act to: (1) increase to 20 percent the Medicare bonus paid to physicians for primary care in an underserved area; and (2) extend bonus payments for a period of three years after an area loses its designation as a shortage area.

(Sec. 7102) Provides payments for undergraduate medical education to schools that: (1) recruit underrepresented racial or ethnic minority groups; and (2) encourage students to enter the primary care field.

(Sec. 7103) Provides for a study of the funding needs of health professions schools.

Subtitle C: Essential Health Facilities - Provides for the participation of all States in the Essential Access Community Hospital Program. Continues the current level of authorization of appropriations through FY 1995. Increases the level FY 1995 through FY 1999. Makes other changes to the EACH program including changes concerning: (1) the treatment of inpatient hospital services; (2) designation of hospitals; (3) eligibility of hospitals not located in participating States; (4) rural health care plan requirements; and (5) physician staffing. Requires implementation of the prospective payment system for rural primary care hospital services by January 1, 1996.

(Sec. 7202) Creates a grant program for States that have developed or are developing a community health network plan that: (1) provides for the creation of a community health network; (2) promotes the integration of the delivery of health care services; (3) improves access to hospital and other services; and (4) has designated nonprofit or public hospitals and facilities as community health network providers. Defines a community health network as a public or nonprofit entity that provides primary care and acute care services, including health promotion, health maintenance, and disease prevention in a health professional shortage area or in an underserved area.

(Sec. 7203) Establishes the Capital Financing Trust Fund to provide capital financing assistance to eligible hospitals and facilities in the form of loan guarantees, interest rate subsidies, direct matching loans, and grants for urgent capital needs. Requires a hospital, for eligibility purposes, to be: (1) designated as an essential access community hospital; (2) designated as a rural primary care hospital; or (3) one with a disproportiate patient percentage equal to or greater than 40 percent. Requires a hospital, in order to qualify for assistance, to: (1) be owned or operated publicly; (2) be a quasi-public corporation; or (3) be a private nonprofit hospital. Provides for interest subsidies for eligible academic health centers to reduce the cost of financing major facility replacement projects of eligible hospitals.

Subtitle D: Lead Paint Abatement - Establishes a lead paint abatement allotment program for States and certain political subdivisions with contracts being awarded from amounts available in the Lead Abatement Program Account set up under title XI of this Act. Permits contract amounts to be used: (1) to perform risk assessments; (2) provide for the abatement of hazards; (3) monitor blood-lead levels of abatement workers; (4) test blood-lead levels of children; (5) acquire temporary housing for low-income residents of buildings in which abatement activities are taking place; and (6) for other specified purposes.

Subtitle E: Federal Grants for Managed Care Plans - Authorizes appropriations for grants to eligible public and nonprofit private organizations for the development of staff or group model health maintenance and other managed care organizations in designated health professional shortage areas.

Permits an organization to such funds for: (1) market surveys; (2) enrollment of individuals; (3) raising working capital; (4) recruiting health personnel; (5) acquiring buildings and equipment; (6) developing provider networks; and (7) other purposes.

Subtitle F: Emergency Medical Services in Rural Areas - Authorizes appropriations for the establishment of the Office of Rural Emergency Medical Services which shall: (1) conduct and support research; (2) foster the development of appropriate systems of such services; (3) sponsor workshops and conferences; (4) disseminate information; (5) provide technical assistance; and (6) coordinate activities. Authorizes grants to States to improve the availability and quality of rural emergency medical services through the operation of State offices of rural health. Authorizes up to seven grants to States to assist in the creation or enhancement of air medical transport systems that provide victims of medical emergencies in rural areas with access to treatment.

Subtitle G: Biomedical Research Program Account - Provides for grants to eligible entities to conduct a program for the support of biomedical research.

Subtitle H: United States-Mexico Border Health Commission - Authorizes the President to conclude an agreement with Mexico for the establishment of a binational commission to be known as the United States-Mexico Border Health Commission which shall: (1) conduct a comprehensive assessment in the United States-Mexico border area to identify, evaluate, prevent, and resolve the health problems of that area; (2) implement actions recommended by the assessment; and (3) recommend a fair reimbursement method for the Government of the United States and Mexico.

Title VIII: Medicare and Medicaid - Subtitle A: Medicare Part C Program - Adds to SSA a new title XXIII (Medicare Part C; Assistance For Low-Income Individuals) under which the Secretary is required to establish: (1) a new Medicare part C program to provide coverage for the benefit package under title III above for eligible individuals not enrolled under a qualified health plan or entitled to Medicare part A benefits; and (2) premium subsidies and supplemental benefits programs for certain low-income individuals.

Defines an "eligible individual" generally as a U.S. citizen or national or permanent resident who is: (1) a certain part-time, seasonal, or temporary employee; (2) a full-time employee in a business with 100 or less employees that elects to cover employees under Medicare part C rather than a private plan; (3) a non-worker; (4) a recipient of AFDC (Aid to Families with Dependent Children) or SSI (Supplemental Security Income); or (5) an employee with income below a certain level.

Describes the enrollment process, requiring the Secretary to establish procedures for enrollment under Medicare part C, with coverage beginning in 1998 and generally consisting of the same package benefits (including cost-sharing) as applicable to a qualified health plan.

Requires coverage package benefits to be provided by Medicare-eligible providers.

Sets forth payment and administrative provisions, among other things, providing for: (1) payments to providers for certain emergency care services furnished to ineligible aliens; and (2) the use of fiscal agents in the same manner applicable to the Medicare program.

Establishes in the Treasury the Medicare Part C Trust Fund for financing the new Medicare part C program (including low-income assistance) out of the revenues generated from the taxes imposed under title II above and State maintenance-of-effort payments below. Provides for: (1) computation of monthly premiums for individual, single parent, and family enrollment in Medicare part C on a State-by-State basis; and (2) collection of individual premium payments.

(Sec. 8002) Requires the Secretary to: (1) develop and implement prospective payment methodologies for certain services; and (2) revise the current payment methodology for hospital outpatient services for establishing a hospital-specific limit on payments for such services.

Subtitle B: Benefits for low-Income Individuals; State Maintenance of Effort - Outlines: (1) the subsidy program to be established by the Secretary for assisting low-income individuals covered under employer health programs in meeting premium costs through the issuance of premium certificates; (2) the supplemental benefits program for providing low-income "wrap around eligible individuals" with certain additional benefits not covered under the guaranteed national benefit package, including vision care and payment of any package costs-sharing; and (3) State maintenance-of-effort payment requirements.

(Sec. 8103) Adds provisions to Medicare and Medicaid for, respectively, waiving cost-sharing for certain low-income beneficiaries and limiting acute-care services coverage.

Subtitle C: Cost Containment in the Medicare Programs - Establishes on a per capita basis (using the budget baseline computed by the Secretary for 1995) the total estimated amount of expenditures under Medicare parts A through C for health care related expenses, including cost-sharing, for each year beginning in 1996, adjusted at specified rates for inflation and other applicable factors, and allocated among the States and various classes of health care services established by this Act.

(Sec. 8207) Directs the Secretary to establish a national health expenditures reporting system for purposes of carry out this subtitle.

(Sec. 8221) Limits administrative and judicial review under this subtitle.

Subtitle D: Additional Medicare Savings - Amends SSA title XVIII to provide for: (1) reduced indirect medical education, disproportionate share, and inpatient care hospital capital adjustments; (2) limited payment for physicians' services furnished by high-cost hospital medical staffs; (3) various specified changes with regard to Medicare as secondary payer; (4) co-payments for home health services; and (5) readjusted home health services costs limits.

Subtitle E: Minor and Technical Medicare Amendments - Amends SSA title XVIII to: (1) authorize the Secretary to take occupational mix into account in developing Medicare Geographic Classification Review Board (MGCRB) guidelines for determining the area wage index; (2) provide that if labor markets are no longer based on Metropolitan Statistical Areas, the method of calculating the wage index for reclassification would not apply and the MGCRB guidelines may be revised; and (3) require the Secretary to set the labor and non-labor portion of each standardized amount equal to the national average beginning in FY 1995.

(Sec. 8402) Amends the Omnibus Budget Reconciliation Act of 1987 (OMBRA '87) to: (1) authorize appropriations for the rural health transition grant program; (2) make rural primary care hospitals eligible for program grants; and (3) allow hospitals to use program grants for participation in telecommunications demonstration projects.

(Sec. 8403) Revise requirements with respect to hospital psychology services, skilled nursing facilities (SNFs), notification of hospice services availability, qualifications for service on the Prospective Payment Assessment Commission, budget neutral adjustments for changes in payment amounts for transfer cases, hemophilia pass-through extension, and DRG payment window expansion.

(Sec. 8404) Requires the Secretary to: (1) begin collecting the data necessary for computing a wage index based on wages specific to SNFs; (2) conduct a sub-acute care services demonstration project; (3) develop a methodology for implementing a resource-based system for determining practice expense relative value units for each physicians' service; (4) develop and refine the relative values for the full range of pediatric physician's services; (5) use the most recent available data for geographic indices establishment; and (6) study and report to the Congress on the data necessary for geographic indices review and revision and on the relative values for pediatric and other services to determine whether significant variations exist in the resources used for similar services to different populations. Authorizes appropriations.

(Sec. 8413) Revises rules for billing Medicare part B beneficiaries for physician services in excess of the applicable limiting charge involved (extra-billing limits). Imposes new obligations on carriers before making payment. Provides for refunds of excess amounts.

(Sec. 8415) Prohibits the Secretary or a carrier from imposing any fees for the filing of claims for physicians' services, claims errors or denials, administrative appeals, the obtaining of unique identifiers, or response to inquiries concerning physicians' services.

Permits the Secretary to recognize substitute billing arrangements between two physicians under specified conditions.

(Sec. 8421) Requires suppliers of medical equipment and supplies to have a certified supplier number, except with regard to medical equipment and supplies furnished as an incident to a physician's service, in order to be reimbursed under Medicare. Prohibits: (1) a supplier from having a number without meeting prescribed standards; and (2) the issuance of more than one supplier number, except in certain circumstances.

Allows suppliers to distribute to physicians or beneficiaries a certificate of medical necessity containing certain limited information. Requires that any supplier distributing a certificate with such information also list the fee schedule amount and charge involved before distributing it to the physician for completion.

Requires the Secretary to: (1) study and report to the Congress on the effects of the methodology for determining payments for items of durable medical equipment (DME) on the ability of persons entitled to disability benefits to obtain such items; and (2) report to the Congress on prosthetic devices or orthotics and prosthetics that do not require individualized or custom fitting and adjustment.

(Sec. 8422) Places restrictions on certain telephone marketing and sales activities by DME suppliers.

(Sec. 8423) Specifies the circumstances under which Medicare beneficiaries are not financially liable for covered items furnished by a supplier.

(Sec. 8424) Requires the Secretary to: (1) determine whether the payment amounts for decubitus care equipment, transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulators, and any other items considered appropriate are inherently reasonable; and (2) adjust payments for such items if the amounts are not inherently reasonable.

(Sec. 8425) Requires the Administrator of the Health Care Financing Administration to collect and report to the Congress on data on DME supplier costs and analyze them to determine costs attributable to service and product components and the extent to which they vary by type of equipment and geographic region.

(Sec. 8431) Addresses payment adjustments for ambulatory surgical center services and new technology intraocular lenses.

(Sec. 8432) Requires the Secretary to study and report to the Congress on: (1) patient care costs for Medicare beneficiaries enrolled in clinical trials of new cancer therapies; and (2) continuation of the annual limitation on the payment amount for outpatient services of independently practicing physical and occupational therapists.

(Sec. 8434) Authorizes the Secretary to enter into agreements with the States for allowing them to pay the penalties applicable to individuals for late enrollment premium payments under Medicare part B.

(Sec. 8435) Provides that rural health clinics (RHC) and federally qualified health centers (FQHC) are not limited to providing services solely to outpatients. Covers diagnostic X-ray services as RHC and RQHC services.

(Sec. 8436) Requires mammography facilities providing covered screening or diagnostic mammograms to Medicare beneficiaries to hold a certificate (or provisional certificate) issued under the Public Health Service Act.

(Sec. 8437) Changes the terms "speech therapy" and "speech pathology services" to "speech-language pathology services."

(Sec. 8438) Makes miscellaneous and technical amendments, among other things, to: (1) apply outpatient payment limits to diagnostic services; (2) exclude the services of nurse practitioners and clinical nurse specialists from the definition of inpatient hospital services; and (3) allow individuals who have employer group health coverage to enroll in part B at any time they are enrolled in the group health plan, rather than after they leave the plan.

(Sec. 8441) Makes specified changes with regard to Medicare as secondary payer.

(Sec. 8451) Allows the Secretary to recognize any successor exam to the Foreign Medical Graduate Examination in the Medical Sciences for payment of direct graduate medical education.

(Sec. 8452) Requires the Secretary to establish and implement a method for obtaining information from newly eligible Medicare beneficiaries that may be used to determine eligibility for Medicaid payment of their out-of-pocket Medicare expenses.

(Sec. 8453) Amends SSA title XI to: (1) require hospitals and rural primary care hospitals to enter into an agreement with the organ procurement agency designated by the Secretary for the service area in which the facility is located, unless it has obtained a waiver, in order to participate in Medicare or Medicaid; (2) repeal the requirement that peer review organizations (PROs) precertify selected surgical procedures; and (3) revise provisions on the notification of State licensing boards by PROs.

Requires an OTA study and report to the Congress with respect to such hospital agreements and organ procurement and distribution.

(Sec. 8455) Requires the Secretary to: (1) treat as a separate class Medicare beneficiaries with respect to whom there is a primary group health plan in defining classes to be used in determining the annual per capita rate of payment to an eligible HMO with a risk-sharing contract; and (2) submit a proposal to the Congress providing for revisions to the payment method. Requires the Comptroller General to report to the Congress on the proposed revisions.

(Sec. 8456) Requires use of the most recent hospital wage data in constructing the home health wage index for cost reporting periods beginning July 1, 1996.

Extends the limits on liability under the Consolidated Omnibus Budget Reconciliation Act of 1985 for claims disallowed by a lack of medical necessity.

(Sec. 8457) Makes permanent the authority provided under the Deficit Reduction Act of 1984 for the Secretary to enter into agreements with fiscal intermediaries and carriers on other than a cost basis.

(Sec. 8458) Requires the Secretary to conduct demonstration projects for: (1) medical transportation and emergency room treatment for reducing the costs involved; and (2) Medicare coverage of comprehensive diabetes treatment, management, and education services for determining whether the payment for such treatment should be modified.

(Sec. 8460) Amends the Omnibus Budget Reconciliation Act of 1986 to increase the number of authorized PACE sites.

(Sec. 8460A) Provides that user fees imposed under the Clinical Laboratories Improvement Act of 1967 are not subject to Medicare's general ban on user fees.

Modifies the phase-in-schedule under the Omnibus Budget Reconciliation Act of 1993 (OMBRA '93) for Medicare beneficiaries who receive immunosuppressive drugs following on organ transplant.

(Sec. 8461) Makes various technical corrections to provisions relating to Medicare supplemental policies.

Title IX: Quality and Consumer Protection - Subtitle A: Quality Management and Improvement - Directs the Secretary to establish and oversee a performance-based program of quality management and improvement designed to enhance the quality, appropriateness, and effectiveness of health care services to be known as the National Quality Management Program. Requires the program to consist of the following elements: (1) consumer surveys; (2) national measures of quality performance; (3) methodologies for profiling health care providers and the methods and standards for improving quality of care; (4) quality-related profiling data; (5) national quality standards for private plan sponsors; (6) compliance monitoring; (7) guideline development and certification and research on health care quality; (8) contracts with approved quality improvement organizations; and (9) quality management grants made to approved States. Authorizes appropriations.

(Sec. 9012) Directs the Secretary to provide for the appointment of a Health Care Quality Advisory Commission which shall provide recommendations to the Secretary.

(Sec. 9021) Sets forth provisions concerning: (1) the grievance and appeals process under which a claim is made for payment or provision of benefits under a private health benefit plan or for preauthorization of items or services; (2) anti-discrimination; and (3) privacy standards for protected health information.

Subtitle B: Information Systems and Administrative Simplification - Requires each health benefit plan sponsor to issue a health security card for each individual who is entitled to benefits under a health benefit plan provided or sponsored by the sponsor if the plan is the medicare program or provides for coverage of the guaranteed national benefit package.

(Sec. 9101) Directs the Secretary to establish a national enrollment verification system for the verification of an individual's enrollment in a health benefit plan and entitlement in a health benefit plan and entitlement to benefits under such plan.

(Sec. 9103) Establishes standards for uniform claims and electronic claims data. Requires health care providers to submit claims consistent with such standards.

(Sec. 9104) Directs the Secretary to promulgate standards concerning uniform clinical data sets.

(Sec. 9105) Requires uniform hospital cost reporting.

Subtitle C: Fraud and Abuse - Amends title XI (General Provisions and Peer Review) of the Social Security Act to establish additional penalties, increase certain penalties, permit a carrier or sponsor to bring a civil action, and make other revisions to anti-fraud and abuse provisions applicable to Medicare, Medicaid, and State health programs.

(Sec. 9212) Creates the All-Payer Health Care Fraud and Abuse Control Account in the Treasury the funds of which shall be available to carry out the All-Payer Health Care Fraud and Abuse Control Program which shall be a program to coordinate prevention, detection, and control of health care fraud and abuse.

(Sec. 9221) Applies, generally, Medicare and Medicaid fraud and abuse provisions to fraud and abuse violations of other payers in the national health care system.

(Sec. 9231) Directs the Secretary to establish a process which the Secretary, upon request, will issue an advisory opinion concerning kickbacks and self-referrals.

(Sec. 9241) Preempts any State law that prohibits a corporation from practicing medicine.

Subtitle D: Physician Ownership and Referral - Revises the Medicare provisions concerning physician ownership and referral. Applies such Medicare provisions to items and services furnished under any qualified health plan in the same manner as such provisions apply to designated health services under Medicare.

Title X: Long-Term Care - Subtitle A: Long-Term Care Program - Adds a now title to the Social Security Act, Title XXIV - Long-Term Care Program for Home and Community-Based Services. Directs the Secretary to establish a long-term care program to provide home and community-based services for individuals with severe disabilities without regard to age or income through approved State plans. Defines an individual with severe disabilities as any individual within one or more of the following categories: (1) individuals requiring help with daily living activities; (2) individuals with severe cognitive or mental impairment; (3) individuals with severe or profound mental retardation; and (4) severely disabled children. Requires a determination of eligibility to be made by entities specified under the State plan using a uniform protocol consisting of an initial screening and assessment specified by the Secretary. Provides for a reassessment at least on an annual basis. Defines home and community-based services to include: (1) agency-administered and consumer-directed personal assistance services; (2) case management; (3) homemaker and chore assistance; (4) home modifications; (5) respite services; (6) assistive services; (7) adult day services; (8) habilitation and rehabilitation; (9) supported employment; (10) home health services; and (11) other care or services determined by a State that will help severely disabled individuals remain in their homes and communities. Excludes: (1) room and board; (2) services furnished in a hospital, nursing facility, intermediate care facility for the mentally retarded, or other specified institutional settings; and (3) items and services to the extent coverage is provided under a qualified health plan or under Medicare. Sets forth cost sharing requirements. Prohibits cost sharing for those individuals with income less than 150 percent of the Federal poverty level and provides for a sliding scale for the remainder.

Authorizes payments to a State with an approved plan of an amount equal to the sum of the following: (1) 100 percent match for the first 20 percent of the State allocation; (2) 6/7 match between 30 and 100 percent of the allocation; and (3) 100 percent match for residual Federal funds. Authorizes appropriations.

Subtitle B: Federal Standards for Private Long-Term Care Insurance Policies - Adds a new title to the Social Security Act, Title XXV - Federal Standards for Private Long-Term Care Insurance Policies. Prohibits the sale of any long-term care insurance policy unless it has been approved in accordance with provisions of title XXV. Directs the Secretary to establish an approval process. Requires a State program, on order to be approved, to provide for the monitoring of insurers and policies by: (1) policy review and certification; (2) reporting by insurers; (3) data collection; and (4) marketing oversight. Requires the State program to provide procedures for the investigation and resolution of consumer complaints. Requires a plan to ensure that the State insurance commissioner has enforcement authorities, including prohibiting the sale of a noncomplying policy.

Directs the Secretary to promulgate regulations, all of which must include specified minimum requirements: (1) designed to standardize formats and terminologies used in long-term care policies and to establish such other requirements as may be appropriate to promote consumer understanding and facilitate comparison of benefits; (2) establishing requirements with respect to the terms of and benefits under long-term care insurance policies; (3) establishing requirements with respect to inflation; (4) establishing requirements with respect to nonforfeiture benefits; (5) establishing requirements applicable to the sale or offering for sale of long-term care insurance policies; (6) establishing requirements applicable to the renewal, replacement, conversion, and cancellation of long-term care policies; and (7) establishing requirements with respect to claims for and payment of benefits under long-term care policies.

Title XI: Revenue Provisions - Subtitle A: Increase in Excise Taxes on Tobacco Products - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to increase the excise taxes on cigarettes and other tobacco products.

(Sec. 11103) Imposes an excise tax on the manufacture or importation of roll-your-own tobacco.

Subtitle B: Treatment of Employer-Provided Health Care - Prohibits health benefits from being provided under cafeteria plans or flexible spending arrangements other than medical savings accounts. Provides for the establishment of such savings accounts to be to used to pay qualified medical expenses. Excludes employer payments to such accounts from their employment tax base.

(Sec. 11202) Makes permanent the deduction for health insurance costs of self-employed individuals. Increases such deduction to 80 percent of medical insurance costs (currently, 25 percent).

Subtitle C: Extending Medicare Coverage of, and Application of Hospital Insurance Tax to, All State and Local Government Employees - Provides for extending Medicare coverage and applying the hospital insurance tax to all State and local government employees.

Subtitle D: Treatment of Organizations Providing Health Care Services and Related Organizations - Sets forth qualification and disclosure requirements for tax-exempt hospitals and other entities providing health care services. Establishes excise taxes for failure to meet such requirements.

(Sec. 11403) Sets forth rules for taxing nonprofit health care organizations and exempts regional alliances from income tax.

Provides for the taxing of health insurance companies as other than life insurance companies.

(Sec. 11406) Provides a tax exemption for high-risk insurance pools.

Subtitle E: Treatment of Accelerated Death Benefits Under Life Insurance Contracts - Provides for the exclusion from gross income of amounts received under a life insurance contract on an individual who is terminally ill.

Subtitle F: Employment Status Provisions - Requires the Secretary of the Treasury to submit to specified congressional committees a legislative proposal relating to the classification of workers as employees or independent contractors.

(Sec. 11602) Increases the penalty for failure to file correct returns involving payments for services.

Subtitle G: Tax Treatment of Funding of Retiree Health Benefits - Requires additional reserves for post-retirement medical and life insurance benefits to cover not less than ten years of the working lives of covered employees and to be maintained as separate accounts.

Subtitle H: Excise Taxes on Insured and Self-Insured Health Plans - Imposes an excise tax on the premiums received under each health insurance policy and on each amount received for health-related administrative services. Imposes an excise tax on accident and health coverage expenditures and direct administrative expenditures under a self-insured health plan.

Subtitle I: Other Provisions - Allows a tax credit for certain qualified individuals who provide primary health services full time in a health professional shortage area.

(Sec. 11902) Increases the allowable depreciation deduction for expensing certain medical equipment.

(Sec. 11911) Establishes the Health-Related Programs Trust Fund consisting of: (1) a Lead Paint Abatement Program Account; (2) a Biomedical Research Program Account; (3) a Health Care Workforce Account; and (4) an Undergraduate Medical Education Program Account. Makes appropriations to the Lead Paint Abatement Program Account and the Undergraduate Medical Education Program Account. Provides funding to the other accounts through excise taxes imposed by this Act.
